doc.title: Germaine Bazzle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: Ear training, sight singing and playing bass
summary: A good ear helped her formal study; she began bass around twelve.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Did you have any trouble when you started formal music lessons with the fact that you had — I’m guessing that you had developed a very good ear by the time you started doing that. Was that a help or a hindrance?

It was a help. It helped with the sight singing, and then too it helped because I played the bass. That also helped the ear you know. I started playing the bass when I was about twelve okay. And all of those things just helped me to develop a fairly decent ear.
